title: One-Pot Lebanese Lamb Stew with Garbanzo Beans
summary: Rooted in Levantine homestyle cooking, this one-pot simmered lamb dish delivers comforting warmth through aromatic warmth and hearty pulses. Tender cubes of lamb shoulder are seared in olive oil directly in a deep Dutch oven, creating a rich savory glaze on the bottom of the pot. Ground cinnamon, allspice, cumin, and coriander are bloomed alongside yellow onions and sweet garlic to build a fragrant spice foundation. Stewed tomatoes, cooked garbanzo beans, and tender baby zucchini join the lamb as it simmers gently into fork-tender perfection. Cooking every component inside a single pot locks in essential nutrients and allows the broth to thicken naturally without added starches. Finished with a splash of fresh lemon juice and chopped flat-leaf parsley, the stew strikes a harmonious balance between deep savory spices and bright herbal notes. Pair this nourishing meal with warm flatbread or fluffy bulgur to soak up every drop of spice-scented tomato broth.

steps.step: Trim excess surface fat from lamb shoulder and cut meat into uniform one-inch cubes.
Pat lamb cubes thoroughly dry using paper towels to ensure effective browning in oil.
Season lamb cubes evenly with salt and freshly cracked black pepper in large bowl.
Dice yellow onions, carrot, and celery into small matching dice for cooking base.
Mince fresh garlic cloves finely and slice zucchini into half-inch thick half-moons.
Heat olive oil over medium-high heat in a large heavy Dutch oven until shimmering.
Place half of seasoned lamb cubes into hot oil in single layer without crowding pan.
Sear lamb cubes for six minutes, turning occasionally until deep brown on all sides.
Transfer browned lamb to plate using slotted spoon, keeping hot fat inside Dutch oven.
Repeat searing process with remaining lamb cubes, transferring batch to plate when done.
Add chopped yellow onions, carrot, and celery to remaining fat inside Dutch oven.
Sauté diced vegetables over medium heat for five minutes until onions turn soft and translucent.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste to vegetables, cooking two minutes until paste darkens.
Stir ground cinnamon, allspice, cumin, and coriander into vegetables until fragrant.
Return seared lamb cubes along with accumulated juices back into Dutch oven pot.
Pour diced tomatoes with their juice and beef broth directly into Dutch oven.
Add bay leaf, red pepper flakes, and pomegranate molasses, stirring well to combine.
Bring stew liquid to a full boil over high heat, stirring bottom to prevent sticking.
Reduce heat to low, cover pot with tight lid, and simmer gently for forty-five minutes.
Drain and rinse garbanzo beans in colander under cold tap water to remove canning liquid.
Uncover pot after forty-five minutes and test lamb for initial fork tenderness.
Stir rinsed garbanzo beans and sliced zucchini half-moons directly into simmering stew.
Cover pot again and simmer over low heat for fifteen minutes until zucchini turns soft.
Toast pine nuts in a small dry skillet over medium heat for three minutes until golden.
Uncover pot and let stew simmer uncovered for five minutes to thicken sauce slightly.
Discard bay leaf from stew pot using metal tongs and skim off any surface fat.
Stir fresh lemon juice into hot stew broth to lift rich spices with clean acidity.
Taste broth carefully and adjust seasoning with extra salt or black pepper if needed.
Finely chop fresh flat-leaf parsley and mint leaves on clean cutting board.
Ladle hot lamb stew evenly into six wide soup bowls, sharing meat and beans equally.
Ensure each serving receives ample warm spice broth and tender zucchini pieces.
Sprinkle toasted pine nuts evenly over each bowl of hot stew for crunchy texture.
Garnish stew bowls with chopped parsley and mint leaves just before bringing to table.
Dust a pinch of tart sumac powder over top of each bowl for vibrant red contrast.
Serve immediately alongside warm pita bread or steamed bulgur wheat for dipping.
Provide extra lemon wedges on side plate for guests who prefer brighter citrus notes.
Store leftover stew in airtight container in refrigerator for up to three full days.
Reheat leftovers gently in covered pot over medium-low heat, adding broth if needed.
Check seasoning of reheated leftovers as flavor profile deepens during cold storage.
Sprinkle fresh herbs over reheated portions to restore bright visual color contrast.
Pair stew with crisp cucumber salad to offer fresh crunch against warm spices.
Serve hot stew bowls promptly while fragrant steam lifts spice aromas into air.
